extracted.intended_audience: parties to Investigation No. 337-TA-1362 (Complainants, Respondents, OUII), interested government agencies, and other interested persons (e.g., importers, third parties)
extracted.subtask_description: Prepare and file written submissions responding to specified legal questions on Commission review (invalidity, written description, procedural rules) and submissions addressing remedy, the public interest, and bonding in a Section 337 investigation. Submissions must meet the Commission's content, formatting, confidentiality, and page/deadline requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 1: Timing and sufficiency of invalidity contentions disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: How and when did Respondents and OUII disclose their invalidity contentions? Was this sufficient notice to Complainants, and how did Complainants respond to these disclosures?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties are requested to brief with reference to the applicable law and the existing evidentiary record and provide citations to where these facts and arguments were presented to the CALJ in connection with Complainants' motion in limine no. 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 2: Overlap of written description with claim construction/non-infringement
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether and to what extent the substance of Respondents' and OUII's written description arguments overlap with their claim construction and non-infringement arguments; whether the written description arguments are contingent on the CALJ-adopted construction of 'trifurcated connector body'; and whether full bases for the alleged written description defense were timely disclosed prior to close of fact and expert discovery.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Brief positions with references to law and evidentiary record; provide citations to where presented to the CALJ in connection with Complainants' motion in limine no. 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 3: Discovery regarding lack of written description
rubrics_metrics.description: Did the parties propound discovery requests and produce discovery regarding the alleged lack of written description under 35 U.S.C. 112? What discovery was produced by each party? Did these discovery responses provide adequate and timely notice of this affirmative defense?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify specific discovery requests/responses and explain adequacy and timeliness as notice of the defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 4: OUII questioning of Mr. Merchant on written description defense
rubrics_metrics.description: After Mr. Merchant testified that Summit did not assert any invalidity defense, did OUII question Mr. Merchant regarding any alleged written description invalidity defense?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State whether such questioning occurred and cite record where it was presented to the CALJ.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 5: Effect of Respondents' pro se status
rubrics_metrics.description: How should Respondents' pro se status affect the Commission's consideration of Respondents' briefing and representations as to Respondents' alleged written description defense? Discuss leniency for pro se litigants under Federal Circuit and Supreme Court precedent, and how courts consider prejudice/harm when a pro se litigant fails to provide adequate and timely notice of an affirmative defense before discovery closes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide legal authority and apply to the facts concerning Respondents' alleged written description defense.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 6: Whether OUII may raise an unpled invalidity defense
rubrics_metrics.description: Should OUII be allowed to raise an invalidity defense that was not pled or disclosed by Respondents? When and in what form was OUII first required to disclose its contention that the '295 patent was invalid based on lack of written description under the CALJ's Ground Rules and the Commission's Rules? If the prehearing brief is the earliest required time, how should prejudice to Complainants be considered? Should OUII be required to respond to contention interrogatories if served by private parties?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Address timing/form of disclosure obligations, prejudice analysis, and procedural obligations of OUII under Commission and CALJ rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 7: Good cause to waive pleading requirements (Rule 210.13(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Is there 'good cause' to waive the pleading requirements under Commission Rule 210.13(b) with respect to Respondents' alleged assertion of invalidity? Did Respondents or OUII argue to the CALJ that good cause existed to waive the requirement that bases of invalidity defenses be pled in the answer to the complaint?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze whether 'good cause' exists and whether such arguments were presented to the CALJ; cite rule 210.13(b).

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 8: Applicability and limits of Rule 210.14(c) (amendment of pleadings by consent)
rubrics_metrics.description: Does Commission Rule 210.14(c) apply to the invalidity contentions asserted by Respondents or OUII? Is Rule 210.14(c) limited to amendment of pleadings to conform to evidence admitted at hearing by consent? Did Respondents or OUII argue to the CALJ that requirements of Rule 210.14(c) were met?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain scope/limitations of Rule 210.14(c) and whether its criteria are satisfied here; cite record where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 9: Harm or prejudice to Complainants from permitting written description evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Discuss any harm or prejudice to the Complainants from permitting Respondents and/or OUII to present evidence at the hearing as to the affirmative defense of written description given the facts from questions 1–8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analyze prejudice/harm and support with record citations and legal standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 10: Relevance of Lannom (Fed. Cir. 1986)
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain whether and to what extent the Federal Circuit's decision in Lannom Mfg. Co. v. U.S. Int'l Trade Comm'n, 799 F.2d 1572 (Fed. Cir. 1986), applies to the facts in this investigation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Compare Lannom's holding and reasoning to the present facts and record; cite the decision and relevant record evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 11: Whether invalidity can be decided on Commission review or requires remand
rubrics_metrics.description: If the Commission reverses the grant of Complainants' motion in limine no. 2, can the invalidity defense be decided by the Commission on review, or should the Commission remand the investigation to the CALJ for further proceedings?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss standards for deciding factual/complex issues on review versus remand and apply to the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 12: Whether Claim 1 of the '295 patent is invalid for lack of written description
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on the present record, would claim 1 of the '295 patent be invalid for lack of written description pursuant to 35 U.S.C. 112 under the Commission's adopted construction for 'trifurcated connector body' and applicable case law?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide analysis applying the Commission's construction and case law to the record evidence; cite the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 13: Relevance of Complainants' voluntary recall to written description
rubrics_metrics.description: Explain the relevance, if any, of the circumstances surrounding Complainants' voluntary recall of the Vial2Bag DC product in assessing whether the written description shows inventors were in possession of an invention covering the redesigned Vial2Bag Advanced device as of the filing date of the '295 patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discuss evidentiary relevance and probative value of recall circumstances to written description inquiry; cite record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Question 14: Additional evidence that would have been presented if motion in limine denied
rubrics_metrics.description: What additional evidence regarding the written description defense would the parties have presented at hearing if Complainants' motion in limine no. 2 had been denied?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specify witnesses, exhibits, testimony, or expert evidence that would have been presented and explain why it is material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limit submissions to discrete issues requested and remedy/public interest/bonding matters
rubrics_metrics.description: The parties are invited to brief only the discrete issues requested above and the issues of remedy, the public interest, and bonding. Parties are not to brief other issues on review which are adequately presented in existing filings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not submit briefs on other issues; focus only on the enumerated questions and on remedy/public interest/bonding matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Identify the remedy sought and submit proposed remedial orders
rubrics_metrics.description: In its initial submission, Complainants must identify the remedy sought. Complainants and OUII are requested to submit proposed remedial orders for the Commission's consideration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If seeking an exclusion order for types of entry other than entry for consumption, indicate and provide information establishing that such activities adversely affect the party or likely will do so. See cited background (Certain Devices for Connecting Computers via Telephone Lines).

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide HTSUS subheadings and identification of known importers
rubrics_metrics.description: Complainants are requested to provide the HTSUS subheadings under which the accused products are imported and supply identification information for all known importers of the products at issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include accurate HTSUS codes and importer details to support remedial relief and bonding calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address public interest factors (four specific factors)
rubrics_metrics.description: Written submissions addressing the public interest should consider the effect that an exclusion order and cease and desist orders would have on: (1) public health and welfare, (2) competitive conditions in the U.S. economy, (3) U.S. production of like or directly competitive articles, and (4) U.S. consumers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain how these factors apply in the context of this investigation and provide supporting facts/evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Address bonding amount and bonding-related submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should address the amount of the bond that should be imposed if a remedy is ordered, given that the U.S. Trade Representative has 60 days to act and subject articles would be entitled to enter the United States under bond during that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explain and justify proposed bond amounts, considering the potential period for importation under bond and Treasury/Commission practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Page limits and deadlines for initial and reply submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial written submissions and proposed remedial orders must be filed no later than close of business on May 30, 2024. Reply submissions must be filed no later than close of business on June 10, 2024. Opening submissions are limited to 80 pages; reply submissions limited to 50 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No further submissions on these issues will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electronic filing requirements and reference to investigation number
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons filing written submissions must file the original document electronically on or before the deadlines. Submissions should refer to the investigation number ('Inv. No. 337-TA-1362') in a prominent place on the cover page and/or the first page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Commission's paper filing requirements in 19 CFR 210.4(f) are currently waived. See Handbook for Electronic Filing Procedures for detailed instructions. Contact the Secretary (202-205-2000) with filing questions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidential submissions procedure and redacted public version
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person desiring to submit a document in confidence must request confidential treatment by marking each document with a header indicating it contains confidential information; a redacted non-confidential version must be filed simultaneously and served per Commission rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This marking satisfies the request procedure under Rules 201.6(b) and 210.5(e)(2). Non-parties wishing to submit confidential comments must serve those comments on the parties pursuant to the applicable Administrative Protective Order. Redacted non-confidential versions must be served per Rule 210.4(f)(7)(ii)(A).

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and use/disclosure of submitted information
rubrics_metrics.description: All nonconfidential written submissions will be available for public inspection on EDIS. All information submitted (including confidential business information for which treatment is sought) may be disclosed to and used by the Commission, its employees/offices/contract personnel for developing/maintaining records or internal audits/reviews, and by U.S. Government employees/contract personnel solely for cybersecurity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract personnel will sign nondisclosure agreements. Be aware submissions may be used internally for related proceedings and cybersecurity matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may file written submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties to the investigation, interested government agencies, and any other interested parties are encouraged to file written submissions on the issues of remedy, the public interest, and bonding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-parties submitting confidential information must comply with APO service requirements and file redacted public versions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reference to Commission authority and procedural posture
rubrics_metrics.description: This notice is issued under authority of section 337 (19 U.S.C. 1337) and part 210 of the Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure (19 CFR part 210); the Commission is reviewing in part the Final Initial Determination and requests submissions limited to the questions and remedy/public interest/bonding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should be tied to the legal authority invoked and the limited scope of review noted in the notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formatting guidance: prominent placement of docket/investigation number and electronic original
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions should prominently display the investigation number and the original document must be filed electronically.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: See the Handbook for Electronic Filing Procedures for formatting and filing technical details; electronic filing helps ensure timely receipt and compliance with waived paper requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to justify exclusion for non-consumption entry
rubrics_metrics.description: If a party seeks exclusion of an article from entry into the United States for purposes other than entry for consumption, the party should indicate this and provide information establishing that activities involving other types of entry either are adversely affecting it or likely to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide specific factual support showing adverse effect or likelihood of harm from non-consumption entry activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restriction on further submissions absent Commission order
rubrics_metrics.description: No further submissions on the issues of review/remedy/public interest/bonding will be permitted unless otherwise ordered by the Commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Comply with page limits and deadlines; parties should not expect additional filing opportunities absent explicit Commission direction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contact points and accessibility information
rubrics_metrics.description: For further information contact Edward S. Jou, Office of the General Counsel (telephone and address provided). Hearing-impaired persons may contact the Commission's TDD terminal. For help accessing EDIS email EDIS3Help@usitc.gov.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use provided contacts for filing, access, and accommodation questions; verify official PDFs on govinfo.gov when doing legal research.
